newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DORTMUND V MOENCHENGLADBACH MATCH ANALYSIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DORTMUND V MOENCHENGLADBACH MATCH ANALYSIS.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Borussia Dortmund and Borussia Moenchengladbach who meet in the German first division on Saturday (kickoff 1430 GMT):

Playing style: Coach Ottmar Hitzfeld adopts classic German tactics with a libero and fast wing-backs. Libero Matthias Sammer has a very creative role and the freedom to go forward as he did with so much success for Germany during Euro 96. Fellow international Andy Moeller is the main midfield dynamo, operating just behind strikers Stephane Chapuisat and Heiko Herrlich or Karlheinz Riedle. Scot Paul Lambert is the player who does the hard but vital defensive work in midfield.

Strengths: When they are in form Dortmund can produce some exciting football. In Moeller, Sammer and Chapuisat they have players who can turn a match with an individual piece of skill. At the back they have veteran Juergen Kohler, the most experienced defender in German football. Their squad has strength in depth. They and Bayern Munich have the strongest line-ups in the country.

Weaknesses: Lack of consistency. At times they can look a bit hesitant at the back. Despite their success in Europe, they were taken apart in a 4-1 defeat by VfB Stuttgart last weekend. Sammer has just returned from injury and does not have the fitness yet to get forward as much as he would like.

Motivation: Dortmund need to pick up points to keep their position at the top of the table where only two points separate the top four. Despite the fact that they have won the title in the last two seasons, Dortmund do not seem to have lost any motivation to win a third championship. Wednesday's European Cup victory over Auxerre has given them extra boost.

Playing style: Coach Hannes Bongartz plays with a back four. His team can be difficult to play against because they are well organised and able to confuse opponents by varying their positions. Former German international Stefan Effenberg is a vital playmaker. He distributes the ball well and has the ability to land a pass at a team mate's feet from any distance. Swedish striker Martin Dahlin is regarded as one of the best goal poachers in the country when he is playing well.

Strengths: Moenchengladbach are playing much better than they did in the first half of the season and this has given them a psychological boost. They have the recent experience of playing in Europe and know they are a better team than their 13th position in the Bundesliga suggests. When Effenberg is playing at his best, Moenchengladbach can play attractive football.

Weaknesses: They have let in more goals this season than they have scored (28 to 22). They rely too much on Effenberg and when he is absent, it shows. They also have a poor record away from home, winning just one of 12 games.

Motivation: The threat of relegation is a great motivation. Players worry about money and security when they are faced with the prospect of second division football. The game is also a western German derby and the atmopshere will be intense. Moenchengladbach are keen to show that they can still live with the best in the Bundesliga.
